title: Code comments
description: When a comment earns its place, and what it must never contain.

rules.title: Explain why
rules.text: Add a comment only when it explains why, states an invariant or warns about a non-obvious constraint. Skip comments that restate the code.

rules.title: Describe the present
rules.text: Describe the system as it is now. Never narrate the task, the change history or the debugging session that produced the code.

rules.title: No conversation leaks
rules.text: Do not leak prompts, chat history or review back-and-forth into comments, docs or PR text.

rules.title: Self-contained
rules.text: Make each comment understandable to someone reading the file for the first time, without the issue, PR or diff.

rules.title: No section dividers
rules.text: Avoid banner and section divider comments. They go stale and add noise.

rules.title: No tracker links
rules.text: Do not put tracker, chat or ticket links in code comments. Put that context in the commit or PR.

rules.title: Keep human comments
rules.text: Keep helpful human-written comments unless your change makes them wrong. Update them in the same diff.

rules.title: Document public APIs
rules.text: Document public APIs with the language doc format: contract, parameters and the errors callers should handle.

rules.title: Code first
rules.text: Write the code first, then add comments only where it still cannot speak for itself.

rules.title: Reasoned suppressions
rules.text: Give every lint or type suppression a specific rule name and a reason. Prefer fixing the cause.

rules.title: Examples in doc comments
rules.text: Include a tiny example in a doc comment when the usage is not obvious from the signature.
